input.content: Settings client (client.py save_settings) — P0 pattern: client increments that add a new protocol requirement (e.g. require "applied" receipt) unconditionally break the released provider at tag eval-release, whose provider/settings.py update_settings returns only {"ok": True}. Worse, the provider has already stored values when the client raises, so caller sees failure for an applied save. Unit tests used a fake `send` returning the NEW contract ({"ok": True, "applied": True}), masking the incompatibility. Review rule for this repo: every client change must be checked against `git show eval-release:provider/settings.py`; new protocol behaviour must be gated (e.g. behind enhanced_settings) or tolerate absent fields; tests should include a fake mirroring the released provider response.
